text: Because the model did not identify a specific, verified change that would instantly flip the decision, you can focus on broader steps that usually improve a credit‑risk profile. First, try to lower any existing balances; paying down credit‑card or loan amounts reduces the portion of credit you’re using and shows you can manage debt. Second, keep new borrowing to a minimum—avoid taking out additional loans or opening new accounts while you’re working on repayment. Third, maintain steady employment or a reliable source of income, as consistent earnings reassure lenders. Fourth, consider consolidating high‑interest debt into a single, lower‑rate payment to make repayment easier. Finally, keep older credit accounts open and in good standing, as a longer, positive history can boost your overall rating. These actions can gradually lower your default probability and increase the chance of approval.
